headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP interaction from Gemini CLI can cascade into unsafe actions; LlamaFactory is inert but does not reduce the pair’s default danger.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI ingests files, stdin/stdout, and user-configured MCP outputs by default, so malicious content can be treated as instructions. LlamaFactory has no file or MCP surfaces, so it is not itself a bridge, but Gemini’s permissive tool-use path makes prompt injection plausible when paired with content it reads from shared files or MCP servers.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI reads attacker-controlled repo files or MCP responses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP server is introduced between the agents, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not strictly needed.
Review and sanitize any file content before Gemini CLI consumes it.
Use a read-only workspace for untrusted inputs.
Separate agent inputs into distinct directories.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for MCP/file content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can read local files and send context to Google APIs, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem, network, or API surfaces in this profile. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, so leakage between the pair is limited; the main risk is Gemini exposing local files it reads, not cross-agent exfiltration.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Gemini CLI’s working directory, they may be transmitted to its backend.
IF both agents are later pointed at the same workspace, cross-agent leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared working directory.
Run Gemini CLI in a dedicated sandboxed folder.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; LlamaFactory cannot write, modify git, or use MCP. Because only one agent has mutable capabilities, direct write-write conflict is not present in the current pair, though Gemini can still overwrite shared files if the environment later grants LlamaFactory write access.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is later wrapped with write or git permissions, concurrent mutation conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same repo and Gemini runs unsafely, it can clobber shared state.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Use git branches per agent.
Make the shared repo read-only for LlamaFactory.
Snapshot the workspace before Gemini edits.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce tool-using outputs from files and MCP inputs, and LlamaFactory is a model stack that could be used to consume or transform those outputs. The profile does not document verification between them, so if LlamaFactory is downstream of Gemini, unverified instructions or facts can cascade into incorrect support responses or actions.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes Gemini-generated text without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF Gemini is allowed to act on untrusted file or MCP content, downstream outputs may be corrupted.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require citations or structured outputs from Gemini.
Have LlamaFactory validate claims against source data.
Log and diff intermediate outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and a Google API path, while LlamaFactory shows no data classes, residency, or retention commitments in this profile. No explicit mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to unknowns rather than a proven breach; the absence of B-side controls prevents a higher finding.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Gemini CLI’s workspace, residency and retention obligations must be checked.
IF LlamaFactory is used to process the same regulated data, missing policy details become relevant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair’s workspace.
Review vendor retention terms before use.
Document data categories allowed for each agent.
Keep audit logs of transfers between agents.
requires-engineering: define residency and retention policy mappings.
